captions.instagram:
What is resonance?

Push a swing in time and it flies. Shake a spring at its own beat and a 5 mm nudge becomes a 10 cm swing. Tune the shaker, wake a sitar's untouched strings, calm a skyscraper with a 660-tonne ball, and find out what really brought down the Tacoma Narrows Bridge.

→ Pull a mass on a spring and let go. It rings at its own natural frequency, every time.
→ Shake it by 5 mm at that frequency and each push adds to the last: resonance.
→ A pendulum is the same idea: gravity is its spring, and only its length sets the beat.
→ Push a swing once per swing and small shoves add up. Push at the wrong rhythm and they cancel.
→ Play one note on a sitar and the untouched strings tuned to it ring by themselves.

Play with it yourself. It's free and open source: glassbox.how/resonanceclear (link in bio)

youtubeLong.title: What is resonance? (interactive explainer)
youtubeLong.description:
Push a swing in time and it flies. Shake a spring at its own beat and a 5 mm nudge becomes a 10 cm swing. Tune the shaker, wake a sitar's untouched strings, calm a skyscraper with a 660-tonne ball, and find out what really brought down the Tacoma Narrows Bridge.

▶ Play with the interactive version: https://glassbox.how/e/resonanceclear/
⌘ Source code (MIT): https://github.com/bdeeps/resonanceclear

In this video:
• Everything has its own beat. A mass on a spring bobs at one steady rate, T = 2π √(m ÷ k), whatever the size of the bob.
• A pendulum is a spring made of gravity. Gravity pulls a pendulum back in proportion to how far it is pulled, so it keeps time like a spring: T = 2π √(L ÷ g), with the mass cancelling out.
• Resonance picks one frequency. A resonator ignores every rhythm but its own.
• Buildings and bridges swing too. A tower sways at about a tenth of a second per storey.
• Three stories, checked. Tacoma Narrows fell to flutter, a wind-fed twist, not to a matching rhythm.
